 From Cheers to Fear: Wall Street Plunges in a Single Day
 Kim Hyunwoo 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.06 07:41 
 View 
 View Count 
 PIP 닫기 
 [Anchor] 
 Overnight, Wall Street plummeted, centered on semiconductor stocks. Concerns that the Democratic Party would strengthen regulations on the AI industry turned into panic, causing the Nasdaq to plunge 5.5% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index to plummet by more than 12%. 
 Correspondent Kim Hyun-woo reports from New York. 
 [Reporter] 
 Wall Street, which had cheered over the Democratic landslide, froze just a day later. 
 The tech-heavy Nasdaq, led by semiconductors and big tech, plummeted by more than 5%. 
 Compared to the all-time high recorded in early October, it has dropped by more than 10% over the span of a month. 
 The S&P 500 fell by more than 4%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped by over 1,800 points. 
 This completely wiped out the gains made the day after the midterm elections. 
 All three major New York stock indexes recorded their largest single-day drops since April of last year, when President Trump announced tariff policies. 
 Selling pressure was concentrated on semiconductor stocks. 
 Nvidia fell by over 9%, and SanDisk, which manufactures memory semiconductors for AI data centers, plummeted by a staggering 20% or more. 
 In addition, Micron fell by 17%, dragging the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index—which tracks the stock prices of major semiconductor companies—down by over 12% in the wake of the fallout. 
 U.S. media reported that roughly 3 trillion dollars—surpassing 4,000 trillion won in Korean currency—was wiped out from the U.S. stock market in a single day. 
 Analysts attribute the sharp contraction in investor sentiment to forecasts that the Democratic Party, having secured control of both the House and the Senate, will 본격적으로 begin regulating data centers. 
 Concerns have grown that if brakes are put on data center construction, demand for AI semiconductors could also decline. 
 [Interview / Jon Ossoff / U.S. Senator from Georgia (Democratic Party) : No data center should be built secretly in any community in Georgia against the will of the residents.] 
 With Wall Street plunging overnight, the domestic stock market today (November 6) is expected to face considerable impact, centered on semiconductor stocks.
